chapter_sections.label: DEFINITION:
chapter_sections.text:
Coal and Petroleum are FOSSIL FUELS - fuels formed from the dead remains of
living organisms (fossils) that were buried millions of years ago under high
pressure and temperature. They are EXHAUSTIBLE NATURAL RESOURCES.

chapter_sections.label: KEY POINTS:
points: Natural resources can be broadly classified into two kinds:
(i) INEXHAUSTIBLE NATURAL RESOURCES: Present in unlimited quantity in nature
and not likely to be exhausted by human activities. Examples: sunlight, air.
(ii) EXHAUSTIBLE NATURAL RESOURCES: Present in limited quantity in nature and
can be exhausted by human activities. Examples: forests, wildlife, minerals,
coal, petroleum, natural gas.
Coal, petroleum and natural gas are fossil fuels.
Fossil fuels were formed from the dead remains of living organisms millions of
years ago.
These are exhaustible resources and must be used judiciously.

chapter_sections.label: ACTIVITY 3.1
chapter_sections.aim: To understand the concept of exhaustible natural resources.
procedure: 1. Divide students into groups of seven each.
2. Further divide each group into three subgroups containing 1, 2 and 4 students.
3. Label them as first, second and third generation respectively.
4. Put one full container for each group on a table.
5. Ask consumers of the first generation from each group to consume eatables
from their group's container.
6. Ask second generation consumers from each group to do the same.
7. Ask students to observe carefully the availability of eatables in each container.
8. If some thing is left, ask third generation consumers to consume it.
9. Observe whether all consumers of third generation got eatables or not.
10. Observe if anything is still left in any of the containers.
chapter_sections.observation: As generations increase, the available resource (eatables) decreases.
chapter_sections.conclusion:
The eatables in the container represent the total availability of an
exhaustible natural resource like coal, petroleum or natural gas. Each group may
have a different consumption pattern. Earlier generations that were concerned about
coming generations left something for them, showing the importance of judicious use.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

chapter_sections.label: ACTIVITY 3.2 (Group Activity)
chapter_sections.aim: To demonstrate how resources get exhausted with increasing consumers.
procedure: 1. Take some containers. Fill them with popcorn/peanuts/roasted gram/toffees.
2. Divide students into groups of seven each.
3. Further divide each group into three subgroups containing 1, 2 and 4 students.
4. Label them as first, second and third generation respectively.
5. These sub-groups represent the consumers.
6. As population is growing, second and third generations have larger number
of consumers.
7. Put one full container for each group on a table.
8. Ask consumers of first generation from each group to consume eatables from
the container of their group.
9. Now ask second generation consumers to do the same.
10. Ask students to observe carefully the availability of eatables.
11. If some thing is left, ask third generation consumers to consume it.
12. Finally observe whether all consumers of third generation got the eatables
or not.
chapter_sections.observation: Resources reduce as more generations consume them.
chapter_sections.conclusion:
Fossil fuels like coal, petroleum and natural gas are exhaustible.
If consumed at current rates, they may not be available for future generations.

sections.label: DEFINITION:
sections.text:
COAL is a hard, black, stone-like substance that is a fossil fuel formed from
dead vegetation buried under the soil millions of years ago.

sections.label: KEY POINTS:
points: Coal is as hard as stone and black in colour.
Coal is one of the fuels used to cook food.
Earlier coal was used in railway engines to produce steam to run the engine.
Coal is also used in thermal power plants to produce electricity.
Coal is also used as a fuel in various industries.
Coal contains mainly carbon.
Coal is also called a FOSSIL FUEL as it was formed from the remains of vegetation.
When heated in air, coal burns and produces mainly carbon dioxide gas.
Coal is processed in industry to get: COKE, COAL TAR and COAL GAS.
STORY OF COAL (Formation of Coal):
About 300 million years ago, the earth had dense forests in low lying wetland areas.
Due to natural processes like flooding, these forests got buried under the soil.
As more soil deposited over them, they were compressed.
Temperature also rose as they sank deeper and deeper.
Under high pressure and high temperature, dead plants got slowly converted to coal.
The slow process of conversion of dead vegetation into coal is called CARBONISATION.
Since coal was formed from the remains of vegetation, it is also called a FOSSIL FUEL.
PRODUCTS OF COAL:
When coal is processed in industry, three useful products are obtained:
(A) COKE:
It is a tough, porous and black substance.
It is an almost pure form of carbon.
Coke is used in the manufacture of steel and in the extraction of many metals.
(B) COAL TAR:
It is a black, thick liquid (Fig. 3.3) with an unpleasant smell.
It is a mixture of about 200 substances.
Products obtained from coal tar are used as starting materials for manufacturing
various substances used in everyday life and in industry.
Examples of products from coal tar: synthetic dyes, drugs, explosives, perfumes,
plastics, paints, photographic materials, roofing materials, etc.
Interestingly, naphthalene balls used to repel moths and other insects are also
obtained from coal tar.
These days, BITUMEN (a petroleum product) is used in place of coal-tar for
metalling the roads.
(C) COAL GAS:
Coal gas is obtained during the processing of coal to get coke.
It is used as a fuel in many industries situated near the coal processing plants.

sections.label: ADDITIONAL FACTS:
sections.text:
- Coal gas was used for street lighting for the first time in London in 1810 and
in New York around 1820.
- Now a days, it is used as a source of heat rather than light.

fossil fuels.

sections.label: DEFINITION:
sections.text:
PETROLEUM is a dark oily liquid with an unpleasant odour, found between the rocks
under the Earth's surface. It is a natural resource formed from organisms living
in the sea millions of years ago. The word petroleum is derived from PETRA (rock)
and OLEUM (oil) as it is mined from between the rocks under the Earth.

sections.label: KEY POINTS:
points: Petroleum is used as a fuel in light automobiles such as motor cycles, scooters
and cars.
Heavy motor vehicles like trucks and tractors run on diesel.
Petrol and diesel are obtained from a natural resource called petroleum.
Petroleum is derived from petra (rock) and oleum (oil).
Petroleum is also called BLACK GOLD due to its great commercial importance.
Petroleum is also called a FOSSIL FUEL.
The process of separating the various constituents/fractions of petroleum is
known as REFINING.
Refining is carried out in a PETROLEUM REFINERY.
Various substances obtained from petroleum and natural gas are termed
PETROCHEMICALS.
In India, oil is found in Assam, Gujarat, Mumbai High and in the river basins
of Godavari and Krishna.
FORMATION OF PETROLEUM:
Petroleum was formed from organisms living in the sea.
As these organisms died, their bodies settled at the bottom of the sea and got
covered with layers of sand and clay.
Over millions of years, absence of air, high temperature and high pressure
transformed the dead organisms into petroleum and natural gas.
The layer containing petroleum oil and gas is above that of water because oil
and gas are lighter than water and do not mix with it.
REFINING OF PETROLEUM:
Petroleum is a dark oily liquid.
It is a mixture of various constituents such as petroleum gas, petrol, diesel,
lubricating oil, paraffin wax, etc.
The process of separating the various constituents/fractions of petroleum is
known as REFINING.
Refining is carried out in a petroleum refinery (Fig. 3.5).

| S.No. | Constituents of Petroleum       | Uses                                         |
| 1.    | Petroleum Gas in Liquid form     | Fuel for home and industry                   |

| 3.    | Kerosene                         | Fuel for stoves, lamps and for jet aircrafts |
| 4.    | Diesel                           | Fuel for heavy motor vehicles, electric      |
|       |                                  | generators                                   |
| 5.    | Lubricating oil                  | Lubrication                                  |
| 6.    | Paraffin wax                     | Ointments, candles, vaseline etc.            |
| 7.    | Bitumen                          | Paints, road surfacing                       |

sections.label: ADDITIONAL FACTS:
sections.text:
- Many useful substances are obtained from petroleum and natural gas. These are
termed as PETROCHEMICALS.
- They are used in the manufacture of detergents, fibres (polyester, nylon,
acrylic etc.), polythene and other man-made plastics.
- Hydrogen gas obtained from natural gas is used in the production of fertilisers
(urea).
- The world's first oil well was drilled in Pennsylvania, USA, in 1859.
- Eight years later, in 1867, oil was struck at Makum in Assam.

sections.label: DEFINITION:
sections.text:
NATURAL GAS is a very important fossil fuel. It is stored under high pressure as
COMPRESSED NATURAL GAS (CNG). It is easy to transport through pipes.

sections.label: KEY POINTS:
points: Natural gas is a very important fossil fuel.
It is easy to transport through pipes.
Natural gas is stored under high pressure as COMPRESSED NATURAL GAS (CNG).
CNG is used for power generation.
CNG is now being used as a fuel for transport vehicles because it is less
polluting. It is a CLEANER FUEL.
The great advantage of CNG is that it can be used directly for burning in
homes and factories where it can be supplied through pipes.
A network of pipelines exists in Vadodara (Gujarat), some parts of Delhi and
other places.
Natural gas is also used as a starting material for the manufacture of a number
of chemicals and fertilisers.
India has vast reserves of natural gas.
Natural gas has been found in Tripura, Rajasthan, Maharashtra and in the
Krishna Godavari delta.

sections.label: ADDITIONAL FACTS:
sections.text:
- Can coal, petroleum and natural gas be prepared in the laboratory from dead
organisms? No. Their formation is a very slow process and conditions for their
formation cannot be created in the laboratory.

sections.text:
EXHAUSTIBLE NATURAL RESOURCES are natural resources like coal, petroleum and
natural gas that are present in limited quantities and can be exhausted by human
activities. They must be used judiciously (wisely).

sections.label: KEY POINTS:
points: Coal and petroleum are fossil fuels.
It required the dead organisms millions of years to get converted into these
fuels.
On the other hand, the known reserves of these will last only a few hundred
years.
Moreover, burning of these fuels is a major cause of AIR POLLUTION.
Their use is also linked to GLOBAL WARMING.
It is therefore necessary that we use these fuels only when absolutely necessary.
This will result in better environment, smaller risk of global warming and
their availability for a longer period of time.
In India, the Petroleum Conservation Research Association (PCRA) advises
people how to save petrol/diesel while driving.

sections.label: EXERCISE 3 (Chapter Exercise Q3):
sections.raw:
Q: Describe how coal is formed from dead vegetation. What is this process called?
A: About 300 million years ago, the earth had dense forests in low lying wetland
areas. Due to natural processes like flooding, these forests got buried under the
soil. As more soil deposited over them, they were compressed. The temperature also
rose as they sank deeper and deeper. Under high pressure and high temperature,
dead plants got slowly converted to coal. This slow process of conversion of dead
vegetation into coal is called CARBONISATION.

Q: Tick True/False against the following statements.
(a) Fossil fuels can be made in the laboratory. (T/F)
(b) CNG is more polluting fuel than petrol. (T/F)
(c) Coke is almost pure form of carbon. (T/F)
(d) Coal tar is a mixture of various substances. (T/F)
(e) Kerosene is not a fossil fuel. (T/F)

A:
(a) FALSE - Fossil fuels cannot be made in the laboratory. Their formation
conditions of millions of years of pressure and temperature cannot be created.
(b) FALSE - CNG is LESS polluting than petrol. It is a cleaner fuel.
(c) TRUE - Coke is an almost pure form of carbon.
(d) TRUE - Coal tar is a mixture of about 200 substances.
(e) FALSE - Kerosene IS a fossil fuel as it is obtained from petroleum which is
a fossil fuel.
